news.title: US tobacco firms used cigarette-selling tactics to globally market ultra-processed foods
news.summary_en: A new study from the University of Kansas details how U.S. tobacco corporations expanded into global food markets from the mid-1980s to the mid-2000s, using strategies honed through cigarette sales to market ultra-processed foods, which are industrially processed and contain ingredients and additives that maximize their appeal.

news.title: More than a century of KU student journalism now freely available online
news.summary_en: KU Libraries have digitized more than 140 years of University of Kansas student newspapers, from the first campus publication in 1878 through 2017, making the collection freely available through Kenneth Spencer Research Library’s digital repository.

news.title: Studies show that mentoring can also benefit the mentors decades after experiences
news.summary_en: Mary Fry, professor of educational psychology at KU, has co-written two studies that examined mentoring programs. One found that the Strong Girls program benefited those providing the guidance to young girls 10 years after their experience, and another found “sideways mentoring” among peers helped scholars for as long as 20 years.

news.title: Research could lead to cheaper, better testing for ‘forever chemicals’ in US drinking water
news.summary_en: A new investigation from the University of Kansas improves detection of PFAS, a family of so-called “forever chemicals” in drinking water supplies. The method, which can measure such trace pollution levels of PFAS in water more quickly and inexpensively than current techniques, recently was published in the open-source journal PLOS Water.

news.title: KU exhibition explores global impact of sports design ahead of 2026 World Cup
news.summary_en: The University of Kansas School of Architecture & Design will present “Shaping the Future of Football,” an exhibition in Kansas City highlighting the region’s global role in sports architecture. Featuring World Cup stadium models, student design work and emerging technologies, the show explores how architecture, data and design are transforming the future of the game.

news.title: American Constitution Society honors KU Law student and chapter with national recognition
news.summary_en: The American Constitution Society has recognized the University of Kansas School of Law and one of its student leaders with national honors for leadership and programming.
